parsed.explanation: No entry condition targets LGBTQ travellers, but exposure begins immediately: a general photo-ID rule at holiday-destination checkpoints is the documented mechanism through which police contact is initiated, and profiling stops of ~20 trans women (Aug 2025) alongside 299 detention decisions in 2025 — 43 off the record — show state-tolerated, documented targeting ahead of any enacted law. If custody follows, the operative regime is birth-sex/segregated placement, strip searches, isolation, ineffective complaints and a Dec 2025 custody death investigated two days later with no witness statements. No non-discrimination law exists, official rhetoric frames LGBT people as threats to children, criminalisation is pending, and remedies are contested but unproven. Mitigation: no trans-specific entry ban and the harshest bill was dropped.

entry_documents.exposure: Original photo ID must be carried at transit checkpoints in holiday destinations (fines, detention warnings). This general rule is the documented mechanism initiating police contact; Aug 2025 mass street/shop/café stops of ~20 trans women, held and background-checked, show identity checks converting into trans-targeted detention.
entry_documents.protection: No visa, entry or border condition applies to LGBTQ travellers as such; no documented document-marker, scanner or anatomy-inspection practice affecting trans visitors (source notes this as unsupported in either direction).
entry_documents.interaction: Checkpoint ID check → mismatch or officer interest → station detention → 'general information gathering' record entry, including off-the-record documentation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 299 detention decisions in 2025 (256 recorded, 43 off the record) within 313 documented violations — 2.5× 2024 — plus systematic privacy attacks. Custody death of a trans prisoner (1 Dec 2025): prosecutors arrived two days later, witnesses not taken, medical response delayed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Lawyers invoke Article 5 of a regional human-rights convention; opposition MP raised the death in parliament; national rights groups demanded independent investigation. No documented judicial outcome.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Street ID stop → background-check detention → record entry → possible prison placement by registered sex with segregated, isolated conditions.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Trans/LGBT prisoners managed by segregation and isolation, not gender-matched placement (a trans man held in a women's prison); arbitrary body and strip searches, solitary confinement with restricted healthcare, refused hospital transfers out of fear, frequent transfers, ineffective complaints that can provoke further violence; no policy or staff training, binary heteronormative administration.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Prison-monitoring profile exists and is published; civil-society penal association observes conditions; demands for changed detention practices.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any visitor-facing detention that escalates to imprisonment enters this same binary custody system.

care_services.exposure: HRT not covered by government healthcare; visitors must arrange and pay privately. A 2025 health circular added 'gender reassignment' to medical-board reporting reasons, closing the 'other' option — a named-category profiling route (primarily resident-facing).
care_services.protection: Sex reassignment surgery recorded as available in several major cities at age 18; emergency care access not documented as denied to trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Medication lapse or emergency care can force disclosure to officials whose reporting categories now name transition.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of government's 'Decade of Family and Population' (from 2026) attacks the LGBTQ movement as a threat to children; draft package would criminalise LGBT people via 'family'/'public morals'; proposed 1–3 year penalty for advocating 'behaviour contrary to biological sex'; Sept 2026 raids placed 162 suspects and 22 organisations/businesses under investigation; exclusion demonstrations officially permitted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discriminatory provisions removed from the 12th judicial package (2026); symbolic same-sex weddings made possible; marriage decided by registered gender, not trans status.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses police profiling and shapes how officers treat an outed visitor or a parent travelling with a child.

minors_guardians.exposure: State rhetoric and enforcement frame LGBT people specifically as dangers to children (Decade of Family; Sept 2026 raids 'protecting children'); broadcaster regulator invokes protecting children and family structure against LGBTQ+ content.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No safeguard, discretion rule or complaint route for a trans traveller accompanied by a minor appears in the record.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans adult with a minor moves directly into the state's child-protection threat-framing, which could intensify stops and scrutiny; specific outcome undocumented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025 (three classified hate killings), transgender people disproportionately affected; Aug 2024 knifing of a trans woman where the perpetrator was released and the victim was referred for arrest — activists cite detention asymmetry as official hate policy; entrenched discrimination noted through 2025 Pride monitoring.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Killings classified as hate killings implies some recording; multi-city rights branches, opposition MPs and a pending case since 2023 show organised response.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault report → asymmetrical policing (victim detained) → no effective remedy for a foreign visitor without local network.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive SOGI/GI non-discrimination law; no direct legal protection on gender identity; rights body case pending since 2023 alleging ineffective remedies; regional bloc finds protection insufficient. Unresolved: whether the draft criminalising package was enacted, and the Article 5 outcome; airport/inspection practice not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Regional human-rights convention invoked by lawyers; opposition proposals (2015, 2013 drafts) and removed discriminatory provisions show contested, partially functioning institutions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Escalating violation counts (313 in 2025) alongside recurring oversight findings indicate remedies that do not change outcomes.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-B, police-initiated identity checks and station detentions are the core exposure, with courts deferential. This dossier is materially lower: detentions are quantified at scale (299 in 2025, 43 off-record), state custody produced a death with a two-day-late, witness-free investigation, prison conditions are abusive, and official rhetoric plus pending criminalisation license the conduct rather than merely tolerate it.

Like 0.45-A, routine checkpoint exposure and lengthy verification drive risk, with scarce legal aid and officials blaming error. This dossier sits below 0.45: it adds a documented custody death, systematic strip-search/isolation regime, quantified detention pattern with off-record holds, an asymmetry case (victim arrested, perpetrator released), and no non-discrimination law at all — not just inconsistent enforcement.

0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention ending in release, written reasons, counsel access and compensation. This dossier is far lower: no trained/regulated screening exists (documented as absent), detention is frequent and partly off-record, custody conditions are abusive, and remedies are contested with no documented outcome.

0.15-A involves a criminalised presentation statute, months in pretrial custody with beatings, coerced confessions and a capital clause. This dossier is higher: no trans-specific criminal offence is in force (the 1–3 year bill was dropped), no prolonged pretrial custody pattern or torture for visitors is documented, and no capital provision applies — but custody conditions and impunity place it above that tier.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime runs in one direction: no entry bar, but universal ID checks at holiday-destination checkpoints are the documented gateway to police contact, and trans people are demonstrably stopped, held and recorded — including 43 off-record detentions in 2025 and mass profiling stops. Escalation leads into a binary, segregated prison system with strip searches, isolation, ineffective complaints and a December 2025 custody death investigated only after two days with no witness statements. Simultaneously there is no non-discrimination law, official rhetoric frames LGBT people as threats to children (sharpest risk for an adult travelling with a minor), criminalisation is pending, and 2025 saw six anti-LGBTQ-linked deaths with one case of the victim rather than the attacker being detained. Contested institutions, a dropped bill and removal of discriminatory provisions are real but documented as not changing outcomes; unknowns (airport screening, draft-package status, Article 5 ruling) are unresolved questions, not protections.
